h1: Turkey business visa from the UK
intro: Travelling to Turkey for meetings, a conference or a trade fair? This page explains the Turkey business visa, who needs one and what to prepare. We check the rules for your passport and apply for you.
eligibility: You are travelling for meetings, conferences, trade fairs, negotiations or site visits
You won’t be paid by a company in Turkey
You have an invitation from the company or event you’re visiting
documents: Passport photo page scan, valid for at least 150 days from arrival
Invitation letter from the company you’re visiting in Turkey
Letter from your UK employer confirming your role and the trip

sections.heading: Do you need a Turkey business visa?
sections.text: British passport holders don't need a visa for business visits to Turkey of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Working in Turkey needs a work permit and visa.

sections.heading: What counts as a business visit?
sections.text:
Business visits usually include:
- Meetings with clients, suppliers or partners
- Conferences, exhibitions and trade fairs
- Negotiating or signing contracts
- Site visits and inspections

They don't include taking up paid work for a company in Turkey. That needs a work visa or permit.

sections.heading: Documents for a Turkey business visa
sections.text: The key document is the invitation letter from the company you're visiting. It should include your name and passport number, the purpose and dates of your visit, the company's address and contact details, and who is paying for the trip. A letter from your UK employer confirming your role helps too.

sections.heading: Turkey business visa help from Manchester
sections.text: We handle Turkey business visa applications for individuals and companies across the UK, including urgent trips. See our [corporate visa services](/corporate-clients/) if your staff travel regularly. Before you travel, read the UK government's [foreign travel advice](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice) for Turkey.

faqs.q: Can I attend a conference on a Turkey business visa?
faqs.a: Yes. Conferences, exhibitions and trade fairs are business visits.

faqs.q: Can I work in Turkey on a Turkey business visa?
faqs.a: No. Being paid by a local company, or doing hands-on work, usually needs a work visa or permit.

faqs.q: What should the invitation letter include?
faqs.a: Your name and passport number, the purpose and dates of your visit, the company’s details, and who is paying for the trip.
